result.title: Beyond SAEs: Consistent Concept Discovery with Sparse Coding
result.summary: Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) explain foundation model representations by decomposing activations into sparse combinations of learned dictionary atoms. However, the learned dictionaries can vary across training runs, limiting the reliability and reproducibility of SAE-based analyses. We propose Consistent Sparse Dictionary Learning (ConSDL), which replaces the standard linear encoder with per-sample sparse coding. This is motivated by our synthetic analysis showing that coefficients from a single linear encoder pass are suboptimal compared with those obtained by per-sample optimization, suggesting that sparse coding is a reliable mechanism for dictionary learning. Across 16 synthetic settings, ConSDL achieves near-perfect dictionary and coefficient recovery. These gains translate to state-of-the-art cross-seed consistency across four vision and language settings, where ConSDL improves dictionary and coefficient consistency by 17.6% and 35.9%, respectively, over the average of six SAE baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ConSDL，将 SAE 的线性编码器换成逐样本稀疏编码，以改善字典与系数的恢复质量，并在 16 个合成设定及四个视觉、语言任务上报告了跨随机种子的字典与系数一致性提升。
AI.relevance_reason: SAE／稀疏字典是解析模型内部表示中概念成分的常用手段，或可为核查 VLM 推理时内部状态是否保留视觉细节与实体关系提供分析工具，但该文不涉及多模态推理或 latent 状态生成，迁移价值需人工验证。
